#1364. Serie A official line-ups: Atalanta vs. Inter

Inter start Djed Spence, Pio Esposito and Marcus Thuram for the trip to troubled Atalanta, with Charles De Ketelaere and Nikola Krstovic.

It kicks off at the New Balance Arena in Bergamo at 19.45 GMT (20.45 CET).

You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from today’s five Serie A games on the Liveblog.

The pressure is on the reigning Scudetto and Coppa Italia holders, who need a victory to keep up after Lazio and Roma wins already on Saturday.

Lautaro Martinez is back in the squad, but not risked in the starting XI after more than a month out with a thigh issue, so Pio Esposito hopes to build on his excellent Italy form in partnership with Thuram.

Ange-Yoan Bonny and Aleksandar Stankovic are out of action, with Piotr Zielinski not at 100 per cent after a knock to the foot playing for Poland.

Curtis Jones has not featured since the former Liverpool midfielder’s injury against Roma on September 19, and is only ready here for the bench along with John Stones, as Henrikh Mkhitaryan steps in.

Atalanta had a disastrous run of results with two points from four rounds, but went into the break for international duty with a positive 1-0 victory away to Monza.

The injury crisis is beginning to finally calm down a little bit, leaving only Isak Hien and Odilon Kossounou on the treatment table, although Gianluca Gaetano and Thomas Kristensen are not ready to start yet.

There was a new problem in the warm-up, as Marco Carnesecchi seemed to sprain his knee and walked off shaking his head, replaced by Marco Sportiello.

Franck Kessie is a boost in midfield with Ederson, while Eljif Elmas and Nicola Zalewski are preferred to Jonathan Rowe and Giacomo Raspadori.

De Ketelaere and Krstovic impressed on international duty, so will be eager to keep that form going here.

Atalanta have a famously awful record against Inter, as the 1-1 draw in March ended a run of nine consecutive defeats in all competition.

La Dea haven’t beaten the Nerazzurri since a 4-1 result here in November 2018, scraping just six draws and 11 losses.

#1363. Dundee rout is best display of my Hearts reign so far, beams Vrancken

Published: 17:25 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 17:35 EST, 21 November 2026

Wouter Vrancken said Hearts’ ruthless 8-0 demolition of 10-man Dundee was his team’s best performance since he took charge at Tynecastle.

Sabah Kerjota and Pierre Landry Kabore both scored twice with Claudio Braga, Sabri Guendouz, Stuart Findlay and a Ryan Finnigan own goal taking the tally to eight without reply.

And Vrancken was naturally delighted that his players had ended a run of three defeats in a row in such spectacular style.

The 47-year-old said: 'The best performance? Of course.

'When you have the confidence of one moment and then you feel the score is getting bigger, you see the players with extra confidence.

'You see the dynamics there and it’s good they feel it works.

Stuart Findlay heads in the eighth to cap a remarkable evening for Hearts at Dens Park

'When it’s 0-0 and 1-0, you don’t feel as confident so maybe you don’t have the bravery to do it or show it.

'Today they did it and hopefully they felt it can work and they can show it more.

'It was ruthless and I like to see it this way. That was the message at half-time – that and keeping the clean sheet.

'I was very happy with the performance, not only the score.

'We had the talks before our days off, they were really honest and open. It was good to hear but you have to take ownership of it on the pitch.

'You can talk as much as you want but if you can’t show it on the pitch it doesn’t mean anything.

'When you do it like this it’s the first step.

'But it’s only the first step, only one game and we have to try to bring more.

“The message to the players is feet back on the ground because after the last break we started with a 5-0 win over St Mirren then had difficult moments.

'It was ruthless in the game today but the schedule is also ruthless – but we got a good boost from tonight.'

Claudio Braga fires home a fifth goal for Vrancken's side in the demolition job

Dundee boss Steven Pressley admitted he was embarrassed by the result and performance.

He said: 'It’s a night I need to own, a night where I can only apologise for the performance. I never expected that.

'I had a little sense we haven’t been quite on it over the last couple of weeks but I take ownership and I mean that.

'We talk about the culture and environment that we set and part of that is making sure we have a fully motivated team, a team which works hard and shows grit.

'We didn’t show that tonight but that is on me and I mean that.

'We looked unmotivated and lacking edge tonight.

'Tactically astute, we were miles away and that’s my responsibility.

'All areas of our performance was disappointing.

#1362. A glucose-powered artificial neuroimmune axis for metabolic control

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature volume 659, pages 647–656 (2026) Cite this article

Metabolic disorders such as diabetes mellitus are global health crises driven by metabolic imbalance, chronic inflammation and dysfunction of the neuroimmune axis1,2,3. Electroceuticals targeting the autonomic nervous system have shown anti-inflammatory effects, yet existing systems lack the metabolic interoceptive feedback to fully restore immune–metabolic homeostasis4,5,6,7,8,9. Here we report an artificial neuroimmune axis (NeuroAxis) as a closed-loop immunomodulatory therapy for treating metabolic diseases. Analogous to its biological counterpart, NeuroAxis is solely powered by endogenous glucose, operating without batteries or wireless power transfer. It emulates the vagal reflex through closed-loop neuromodulation with metabolic interoceptive feedback. In a rat model of type 1 diabetes, NeuroAxis promotes the recovery of insulin-producing pancreatic β-cells and reduces inflammatory immune responses; in a rat model of type 2 diabetes, it drives macrophage remodelling and reduces systemic chronic inflammation. In both models, NeuroAxis restores glucose tolerance, improves insulin sensitivity and normalizes glycaemic control, with therapeutic effects persisting after treatment cessation. Our artificial neuroimmune axis promotes substantial advances in treating metabolic disorders and represents a general approach for autonomously regulating interorgan communication, central to homeostasis and pathophysiology.

#1361. Serie A | Milan 5-1 Frosinone: Magic Manita for Amorim’s side

Milan put in a masterclass of counter-attacking football and tore Frosinone to shreds with five goals, including Goncalo Ramos, Christian Pulisic, and Ardon Jashari’s first for the club.

The Rossoneri had Mike Maignan after shaking off a knock on international duty, but Strahinja Pavlovic was not at 100 per cent, with Matteo Gabbia, Samuel Chukwueze, Fikayo Tomori, Ruben Loftus-Cheek and Alexis Saelemaekers still injured.

The Canarini were in sixth place, just four points behind Ruben Amorim’s side, although they went into the break off a 1-0 defeat to Cagliari after winning three of the previous four. Antonio Raimondo and Florian Grillitsch were still out, plus Gabriele Bracaglia suspended, so they surprisingly moved to a 3-4-3 formation with Romano Schmid as a False 9.

It was a lightning start for the visitors, as after 90 seconds Patrizio Masini’s effort was deflected off Sankhoun Diawara to clip the crossbar at the top corner.

However, Milan opened the scoring moments later when Adrien Rabiot sprung the offside trap on the Luka Modric through ball and rolled across for what was meant to be a Christian Pulisic tap-in, but Gabriele Calvani’s interception just prodded into his own net.

Giorgi Kvernadze tested Mike Maignan at the near post, then on the resulting corner nobody was ready to tap in the Giorgio Cittadini ball flashed across the six-yard box.

Milan doubled their lead with a classic counter-attack, which was started by Goncalo Ramos winning back the ball from Calvani. Diego Moreira sprinted onto the Yunus Musah through ball, rolled across for Rabiot, who in turn set up the Portugal international for a simple tap-in. It was his first goal at club level since October 18.

Frosinone did get back into the game when Kvernadze pulled back from the by-line and it was beyond Masini, but after Fares Ghedjemis only scuffed his attempt, it fell kindly for Masini at full stretch to toe poke it past the on-rushing Maignan.

The referee apologised for not playing the advantage with Goncalo Ramos on goal, as he stopped play to book Cittadini for a foul on Rabiot.

Ardon Jashari was introduced for the second half, moving Musah to left-back, and it paid off immediately with the midfielder’s first goal in the Rossoneri jersey.

Ramos knocked down a long ball for Rabiot, whose through ball sent Jashari running down the left, but rather than roll across for the centre-forward, he blasted it into the roof of the net from a tight angle with the left foot.

Frosinone kept pushing and only a desperate Musah interception prevented Anthony Oyono meeting the Schmid roll across, then Goncalo Ramos went off after feeling a twinge.

His replacement was Alphadjo Cisse, who promptly also scored off the bench. A Frosinone corner was cleared, Pulisic’s cross-field pass sent Moreira running, and Cisse was on target from the through ball. It was at first ruled offside, until VAR confirmed the Italy international was level.

Milan struck on the counter from another Frosinone corner for 5-1, as Pulisic robbed Aleksa Terzic inside his own half to sprint forward and dinked the delicate finish over Palmisani.

Moreira’s finish was too weak to trouble Palmisani on yet another Rabiot assist, and it went from bad to worse for Frosinone. Daniel Birligea didn’t start because he wasn’t fully fit, and limped off with a hamstring issue at the 82nd minute, leaving them down to 10 men with all the substitutions completed.

Milan were practically down to 10 too, as Strahinja Pavlovic made his comeback after illness, but was feeling dizzy and barely jogging for the closing stages.

#1360. He Played For Leeds at 18, Then He Was Sent to Prison For 9 Years

Michael Owen and Frank Lampard are two of the most recognisable names in English football history, racking up 935 Premier League appearances between them, and the pair have naturally had a number of incredibly talented teammates in their time at the very top of the game.

Owen famously won the Ballon d'Or in 2001, after enjoying a prolific season at Liverpool. The pacey striker netted 158 goals in 297 appearances for the Reds, before going on to enjoy stints at Real Madrid, Newcastle United and Manchester United. He finished his career with a Premier League title, an FA Cup and two League Cups to his name.

Meanwhile, Lampard's illustrious career saw him become the most prolific goalscoring midfielder in Premier League history. He hung up his boots having scored 177 goals in the English top flight, whilst he also has a number of team accolades to his name, including three League titles and a Champions League triumph.

While the pair played alongside an array of exceptional, world-class players, there are always teammates that fall by the wayside — not everyone makes it to the very top and stays there. Former Leeds United star Paul Shepherd is among those who played with both ex-England stars and very much falls into this category.

Twenty-seven years after making his first team debut for Leeds at the age of 18, Shepherd was sentenced to nine years in prison.

Born in West Yorkshire, Shepherd joined the Whites' academy at a young age. He steadily progressed through the various youth ranks before going on to make a solitary appearance for the senior side under George Graham.

After uninspiring loan spells at Ayr United and Tranmere Rovers, Leeds parted ways with the full-back, allowing him to leave for the former club in 1999. He'd go on to enjoy stints at Scunthorpe United, Luton Town and Scarborough, as well as spending time in the lower leagues with various semi-professional Yorkshire clubs.

16 years after hanging up his boots, Shepherd's post-retirement life came crashing down when he was arrested and subsequently found guilty of conspiracy to supply Class A drugs.

A defensively astute full-back at youth level, there was some level of excitement over what Shepherd could develop into as he approached the first team. His performances in the Leeds academy were garnering attention, and a month after taking over at Elland Road, Graham chose to acknowledge the defender by calling him up to a matchday squad.

In October 1996, the Whites travelled to North London to take on Graham's former club Arsenal at Highbury. Leeds may have lost 3-0, but the game marked a memorable occasion for Shepherd, who made his senior debut. Completing the entire 90 minutes, the right-back was strangely deployed as a forward, alongside legendary number nine Ian Rush.

Many thought that this game might serve as a launchpad for Shepherd's career at Elland Road, but it proved to be anything but. Graham inexplicably opted to leave the youngster out of the squad for the rest of the 1996/97 season, despite the player being properly integrated into the senior set-up at this point.

“George came into the club, by then I was a professional, and he literally never said two words to me,” Shepherd told Planet Football in 2020.

"As a young kid, you just think ‘he doesn’t like me’. It was really hard to deal with. He [Graham] gave me my debut at Arsenal, but he never spoke to me once during the time I was there, before, during or after that game. Literally nothing. As an 18-year-old kid, I had no idea how to handle it, to be honest. It was a real shock to the system.”

While Graham evidently wasn't fond of Shepherd, this lack of senior minutes at club level didn't prevent the Leeds academy graduate from making waves in the England youth set-up. In the summer of 1997, Shepherd was named in the Three Lions' squad for the FIFA World Youth Championship, held in Malaysia.

The England squad consisted of the likes of Jamie Carragher, Danny Murphy and, of course, Owen. A year or so before that, Shepherd had been mixing it with Lampard in England's under-18s squad.

Despite being on a level playing field with these future stars, the Leeds man didn't develop in the same way some of his peers did. After Graham froze him out, Shepherd attempted to reignite his career in West Yorkshire by twice going on loan. Neither proved successful, and he eventually left his boyhood club to sign for Scottish outfit Ayr United.

His exit from Leeds sparked the beginning of a six-year spell which saw Shepherd play for eight different clubs. After failing to make an appearance at Oldham, he spent time in non-league, at Scarborough, Leigh RMI, Harrogate Town and finally, Stalybridge Celtic.

Shepherd retired in 2005 after struggling to settle at a number of different clubs. In 2023, the ex-footballer was arrested for dealing large amounts of cocaine.

According to BBC News, Shepherd was found guilty of being a trusted courier for the drugs, involved in collecting and delivering cash for linchpin Carl O'Flaherty all over the UK.

The former Leeds star was jailed alongside three other men, with the criminal network uncovered after police stopped Shepherd and seized cocaine from his car. It was unearthed that O'Flaherty had led a wholesale drugs supply business for a number of years, and he was ultimately sentenced to 17 years and 10 months in prison.

Shepherd's sentence was less severe, although he was still jailed for nine years and six months after pleading guilty.

A former Arsenal player, who played alongside Jack Wilshere and Cesc Fabregas, was sentenced to four years in prison back in 2025.

#1359. Forget Garnacho: Emery's Treatment Of Aston Villa Star Ibrahim Mbaye Is Baffling

Aston Villa suffered a disappointing 0-0 draw at home to relegation-threatened Sunderland, making it three stalemates on the bounce.

After going on an impressive run of form, Aston Villa have dropped off of late, throwing away a lead against Manchester United, drawing at home to Fulham, and most recently failing to score against Sunderland.

Their latest performance and result will be particularly disappointing for Unai Emery, with Villa struggling to create too many clear-cut chances.

The Midlands club created just 1.03 expected goals against Sunderland, creating just one big chance.

Sunderland have given up plenty of opportunities so far this season, conceding 17 goals, but Villa failed to find the back of the net.

There's no doubt Villa missed a creative spark in the final third, with the likes of Johan Manzambi and Emi Buendia struggling to produce the goods.

Emery's treatment of certain players has certainly been interesting so far this season.

Taylor Harwood-Bellis's treatment was one that was disappointing in the opening months of the campaign, but he has started to give the former Southampton defender more minutes.

Alejandro Garnacho is another for Villa, with the Argentinian forward struggling to even make the matchday squad at the moment.

The most confusing decision, however, is the fact that Ibrahim Mbaye are yet to start in the Premier League so far this season.

The 18-year-old has played just 174 minutes for Villa this season in the Premier League, despite the Midlands club paying a whopping £47 million to secure his signature.

There's no guarantee that Mbaye is going to be the answer for Villa in the final third, but he is the type of player who can produce magic to turn draws into wins.

Manzambi was shoved out wide against Sunderland to allow Buendia to play in the middle, but the latter has produced just one goal in eight starts in the Premier League this season.

It could be time for Emery to start showing more faith in Mbaye, with experienced players like Buendia not producing the goods.

After no wins in their last five games in competitions, failing to score in three of those games, Emery needs to make some changes.

Summer departures shook Villa's rhythm, while a departed forward is ripping up Serie A with relentless finishing.

It was always going to be a difficult season for Villa with so much change within their squad.

The Midlands club sold so many key players and lots of experienced ones too, targeting younger stars as their replacements.

As a result, things are taking time to gel, and inconsistency has crept in. Despite that, Emery simply isn't getting the best out of his squad at the moment, failing to use certain players for various reasons.

It's unclear why Emery has his favourites and is reluctant to use others, especially when things aren't going too well for them at this stage.

#1358. Pierre Sage fears for his Crystal Palace future after Brighton humiliation

Pierre Sage has admitted that he fears for his future at Crystal Palace, adding that he felt “shame” after his side slumped to their joint-heaviest defeat by rivals Brighton and Hove Albion.

Sage replaced Oliver Glasner as manager in June but since then Palace have won just two league matches with him in at the helm. The south London club have taken seven points from seven Premier League games and have already conceded 17 goals, the most of any team in the league.

“I don’t know,” Sage said when asked if he will get enough time to rectify Palace’s slump. He admitted that his shame was about how Palace were overwhelmed, leaking three goals within the first nine minutes of the game before eventually losing 5-0.

“We are not at the level we expected, and I’m really sorry for that,” the 47-year-old said. “I just want to apologise to the fans because it’s not normal to show this face.”

The Frenchman said that he took full responsibility for the 5-0 defeat, and understood why hundreds of Palace fans left well before the final whistle.

“I cannot blame anybody because we didn’t do the job in a good way,” he said. “I’m responsible for this team, and when the team play as today, it’s not normal. It’s my fault. I understand them.

“Another feeling is about shame because that’s my feeling after the game and from the beginning. It’s not normal to not respect the necessary of this kind of game.”

Sage admitted that he will be assessing how Palace need to rethink their approach in the coming fixtures, beginning with Thursday’s trip to Besiktas in the Europa League.

“The first work to do is on me,” he said. “I’m responsible for what’s happened on the pitch, and I have a lot of work to do because I have to change this kind of thing.

“It’s maybe in the preparation, in the way we give them the motivation to start the game just before in the locker room in the warm-up. We have to analyse that because it’s not normal. And today it was really at the highest level we cannot expect, and that’s the moment to change the thing.”

For all the scrutiny on his back three, Sage urged his entire side to take greater defensive responsibility, highlighting how the team were too passive in pressing Brighton. Palace have struggled to regain the solidity that long characterised the side since the departures of Marc Guéhi in January and Maxence Lacroix this summer.

“The way of defending is not only on the back three; it is for every player, and there are some things to do collectively, too,” Sage said. “When we defend low we struggle a lot.”

Sage joined Palace after a fine campaign with Lens. He led the club to second place in Ligue 1, just six points off Paris St-Germain, and victory in the Coupe de France. Yet, despite Sage’s reputation when he moved to Selhurst Park, his suitability for the Palace job is increasingly being questioned.

Three years ago, Patrick Vieira lost his job after a defeat by Brighton. Now, Sage could suffer the same fate, with doubts growing that he will still be in charge for Thursday’s trip to Besiktas.

“It’s not my decision,” Sage said. “I don’t want to accept the level of the moment if we are able to do better. And today the work is really important to do, and I will do it. It’s my job, and I’d like to change this.”

With only Manchester City and Arsenal above them, Brighton and Hove Albion are entitled to dream of making history. Yet, whatever happens between now and May, one accolade is already surely their own: the goal of the season award.

Diego Gómez’s 56-yard strike will instantly become the stuff of Brighton lore. The Paraguayan’s audacity will be even more cherished for coming against Crystal Palace, who were pummelled 5-0 in the M23 derby.

All Premier League defeats are equal but some are more equal than others. Three years ago, Patrick Vieira lost his job after a defeat by Brighton. Now, Pierre Sage is at grave risk of suffering the same fate. With less venom in attack, especially with Ismaïla Sarr being an unused substitute, Palace’s sole chance lay in counter-attacking. This strategy disintegrated in the fourth minute, when Jaydee Canvot headed Pascal Gross’s free-kick into his own net.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the M23 derby – or El Gatwicko, as the kids call it these days – as high-flying Brighton and Hove Albion host Crystal Palace at the Amex Stadium. Being frank, this is neither the fiercest nor the most storied Premier League rivalry, but few would have imagined when these sides faced off in the Third Division in the mid-1970s that this would ever become a top-flight match-up sandwiched between European games.

Brighton have been outstanding this season and took their league form into the Conference League, thrashing Lithuanian champions Kauno Zalgiris on Thursday night. Fabian Hürzeler was delighted by his fringe players’ performances on Thursday night and may have some selection questions to answer with Jack Hinshelwood and Georginio Rutter finding the net. Brighton are third in the Premier League and were the division’s heaviest scorers after the last round of matches.

Yet the Palace nut has been a tough one to crack for Hürzeler, having not yet registered a win in four attempts. When asked what he enjoyed most about the rivalry, the German said: “Nothing yet, because I didn’t win any games so far. Hopefully on Sunday this changes… I like these games because they’re derbies, more emotions, it’s a rivalry, it’s [us] against Crystal Palace.”

In his pre-match interview Hürzeler admitted to being an admirer of Pierre Sage, and while the Frenchman’s side have failed to match Brighton’s fast start, they rallied impressively to defeat rivals Nottingham Forest last weekend and fought back valiantly away at Lyon, albeit in a losing effort, in midweek. The return of Ismaïla Sarr from injury is a significant boost.

Elsewhere Bournemouth host Sunderland hoping to secure their first Premier League victory of the season. Marco Rose’s side and Tottenham are the only teams still without a win, but Bournemouth have been perfect in the Europa League and will look to transfer some of that momentum into the league. Sunderland scored late to win away at Portuguese side Torreense.

#1356. Ex-Premier League Referee Delivers Immediate Verdict On Leny Yoro Red Card

Things did not go according to plan for Mauricio Pochettino in his first game as Manchester United manager.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss was given one of the toughest tasks of all in his first game in charge, a trip to old rivals Liverpool at Anfield and almost from the outset it was an absolute nightmare for a manager tasked with revolutionising Manchester United.

Eight minutes in, United were reduced to ten men, with Leny Yoro sent off for a clumsy tackle on Alexander Isak as he went through on goal. And then, within five minutes, United were 2-0 down with Dominik Szoboszlai scoring the resulting free-kick and Florian Wirtz volleying home from a Rio Ngumoha cutback.

Ngumoha himself scored in the second half, with substitute Victor Munoz rounding off the route with a fourth late on.

The red card was the big talking point in the match, with questions raised as to whether it reached the threshold for the denial of a golascoring opportunity.

Former Premier League referee Graham Barber thought the right decision was made.

Speaking exclusively to GIVEMESPORT, he said: "I think it was a red card.

"I think everybody in the stadium and most pundits and when I first saw it, I thought it was a red card. and I thought it was, in fact, quite an easy decision."

The discussion has been around the four points that need to be met for it to be considered the denial of a goalscoring opportunity.

Three of those considerations were clearly met, but the question is, did Isak have control of the ball when he was bearing down on goal? Manchester United goalkeeper Senne Lammens was quick off his line and pounced on the ball soon after Iask was brought dow, leading to suggestions Isak would not have got on to his errant touch.

Barber disagreed. He added: "The consideration that the referee has to make, he probably has to make these decisions in a millisecond, so I think people need to understand how quickly that has to be computed through his head.

"The distance between the offence and the goal is one of the things he has to consider. He obviously looks at the general direction of play, and then also whether there are the defenders around him or not, but the one that comes into question is the likelihood of Isak winning the ball.

"Who is to say whether Isak would have got the ball or not? He was running at pace, at real pace at that time. Can you overturn a red card based on that? Highly unlikely, and that's why I don't think VAR was brought into the case because no one will ever know unless a red card was never issued, if the foul was never committed, if he would have got onto the ball.

"In that instance alone, with that particular part of the law, I think the decision was correct."

Manchester United legend was less than impressed after the final whistle against Liverpool

#1355. ‘He Played With Lionel Messi and Neymar - He’s Since Been Given Two Prison Sentences’

Playing for Barcelona, particularly during an era when Lionel Messi spearheaded an attack that also featured Luis Suarez and Neymar, is about as good as it gets for a footballer's career.

Yet, one star who was part of that squad between 2015 and 2020 saw his career completely spiral off course during his time in Catalonia, and is now nowhere near as revered as his Champions League, La Liga and Ballon d'Or-winning counterparts.

The player in question was once considered a wonderkid at Galatasaray, with many fans drawing comparisons between his playing style and that of the great Luis Figo.

A winger and number 10 hybrid who didn't rely on raw pace, but instead used his exceptional ball control and footballing intelligence to become an elite dribbler, he was a rare breed. However, being surrounded by greatness doesn't necessarily mean it will rub off on you.

Having become one of Diego Simeone's most trusted lieutenants following his move from Galatasaray early in his career, 100-cap Turkish international Arda Turan saw his career go up in flames following a big-money move to Barcelona in 2015.

Fresh off the back of a historic treble the previous season, Turan was expected to be the perfect attacking midfielder to slot in behind the iconic MSN frontline. However, due to the club's ongoing transfer ban, Barcelona were unable to register him immediately. Consequently, he didn't make his debut until January 6, 2016 - almost six months after arriving - meaning he was playing catch-up from the get-go.

Yamal has become one of the best players in the world and his former coach has claimed that his talent was undeniable.

Unsurprisingly, he struggled to find his feet, and talk of a potential exit emerged towards the end of the season. Luis Enrique, who had personally pushed for his signing, was nevertheless keen to persevere with the midfielder.

Turan even became the sixth player in Barcelona's history to score a Champions League hat-trick in December 2016, before bagging another treble later that month in a Copa del Rey thrashing of Hercules. However, what appeared to be a turning point ultimately proved to be a false dawn.

As soon as Enrique departed and Ernesto Valverde took charge ahead of the 2017/18 season, Turan's fate was effectively sealed. Out of favour with his new manager, the Turkish international later revealed to beIN Sports Turkey that he felt insignificant under Valverde, having failed to play a single minute during his tenure.

He subsequently left Barcelona on loan to return to Turkey with Istanbul Basaksehir, before making a permanent return to Galatasaray in 2020. He retired just two years later, aged 35, bringing the curtain down on a career that had promised so much. His Barcelona spell ultimately yielded just 15 goals and 11 assists in 55 appearances across five years.

Now, however, Turan is embarking on a new chapter in football, having swapped the pitch for the dugout and taken charge of Shakhtar Donetsk in 2025.

There are no better examples of Turan's downward spiral than the fact he was given two separate prison sentences in the latter stages of his career.

In 2018, Turan became embroiled in a nightclub altercation that left Turkish pop star Berkay Sahin with a broken nose. According to Sahin's wife, Ozlem Ada Sahin, the former Barcelona midfielder had made inappropriate advances towards her before turning on her husband.

Big things were expected from these guys and while some of them more than lived up to the hype, others certainly didn't.

In an even more bizarre twist, Turan later arrived at the hospital where Berkay was undergoing surgery, armed with a gun. He reportedly begged the singer for forgiveness, even telling him to shoot him if he genuinely believed he had harassed his wife.

The incident ultimately landed Turan with a suspended prison sentence of two years and eight months for firing a gun with the intention of causing panic, illegally possessing firearms and intentionally injuring someone, as reported by BBC News.

His second sentence came in March 2024 when he was slapped with a one-year suspended prison sentence and fined roughly €630,000 by a Spanish court after pleading guilty to two counts of tax fraud covering the 2015 and 2016 tax years during his time with Barcelona.

#1354. MOTHERWELL 1 RANGERS 2: Naderi rides to the rescue as wasteful Ibrox men get out of jail with late winner

Published: 18:01 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 18:10 EST, 21 November 2026

FOR a team that just couldn’t find a way to get the ball into the net, no matter how they tried, it was always going to take a couple of jammy deflections or something out of the ordinary to get out of jail.

And that’s exactly how it panned out with just two minutes left on the clock. Rangers, tied at 1-1 and in danger of falling six points behind arch-rivals Celtic at the head of the Premiership, were throwing everything bar the kitchen sink at their hosts.

Balls were being blazed high and wide of the target. Chances were being passed up left, right and centre. It looked like Derek McInnes’ men were destined to rack up a third straight away draw in the league and take the club’s record to three years without a win at Fir Park when, in the 85th minute, substitute Findlay Curtis saw an effort parried by Alex Paulsen, Dujon Sterling blasted the rebound towards goal and Motherwell’s No 1 somehow flung an arm in the air and diverted it onto the crossbar.

It looked like the last throw of the dice. Until Ryan Naderi, who had suffered a miserable evening up to that point, made the difference.

A speculative shot from Badredine Bouanani from the edge of the area whacked off the outstretched boot of Martin Moormann and fell into the Czech internationalist’s path on the right.

His jabbed effort towards goal was nothing to write home about, but it carried just enough juice on it to whack off the hapless Moormann again, change direction and fly into the net.

Messy? Yes. Did Naderi care, though? Not a bit. He ran straight into the Rangers crowd behind the goal and lost himself in the relief and jubilation of a victory rescued from the fire.

That’s all that matters right now. Rangers won to keep up the pressure at the head of the table.

Naderi celebrates his late winner that snatched all three points for Rangers

McInnes applauds the travelling supporters after his side kept pace with Celtic at the top

However, there is a recurring problem with this squad. This game should have been out of sight, but missing chances and lacking that killer instinct manager McInnes demands remains a serious problem.

Just look at the stats. Rangers had 29 shots on goal in this affair and 11 on target. It should have been a procession, really. In the end, they only got through by the skin of their teeth.

There are times when these players look like they couldn’t hit a cow on the backside with a banjo and that is going to trip them up big-time in this title race unless they sort it out tout-suite.

They started like a runaway train in this game and got off to the perfect start with Manny Fernandez heading home from a corner within the first 10 minutes.

The problems started when Naderi, just nowhere as convincing in the role of main striker as he is when played with the likes of Kevin Kelsy, benched last night before a late cameo, up beside him, started missing sitters.

Jake Girdwood-Reich then levelled for Motherwell with pretty much their first forage upfield and it all got way more uncomfortable than it should have been. It is something McInnes is going to have to sort out.

The match started exactly the way McInnes would have wanted following the return from the international break with Rangers in the ascendancy from the first whistle and a goal to the good after eight minutes.

It was also as straightforward and as simple a goal as you could wish to see. One from a set-piece which Motherwell really ought to look back upon with some serious self-reflection. It was just too easy.

Djeidi Gassama had won a corner on the left thanks to a cross being deflected wide by Tom Sparrow. Kim Minsu fired in the flag-kick and Fernandez rose unchallenged to nod the ball home from close range. Like taking candy off a baby.

Fernandez gets his head to Minsu's corner to put Rangers in front early on at Fir Park

Fernandez milked the celebrations in front of the home fans after netting his first goal of the season, but Minsu’s reaction was tinged with the same senses of jubilation and relief.

The South Korean had been getting himself in a twist over failing to deliver an assist so far in his Rangers career. Now he’s off the mark on that front, it’s time for him to satisfy the demands from McInnes for a goal as well.

Shortly after the opener, Naderi, leading the line in front of Minsu, with Kelsy having been left on the bench, should have made it two.

An initial chance fell to the Czech internationalist after a Gassama shot had broken to him in the area. Moormann, however, put in a fine tackle to deflect the ball wide for a corner-kick.

Minsu took charge of that situation and fed it to Gassama, whose shot from a central position was parried by Paulsen.

It fell perfectly for Naderi and he should have buried a close-range header that ended up being cleared by Moormann again.

Fail to take your chances when on top and the prospect of getting yourself into bother is always there — and that’s what happened to Rangers on 21 minutes.

Motherwell had barely been up the park. Barely been in the game. However, they won a corner on the right thanks to some decent forward play from Regan Charles-Cook, on for the injured Ibrahim Said, and made the very most of the set-piece.

Emmanuel Longelo played a short corner to Sparrow who fired a low ball into the area at pace.

Girdwood-Reich timed his diagonal run nicely to move into space in front of a static Olwethu Makhanya and his first-time effort with the right foot beat visiting goalkeeper Ivor Pandur to his right to settle in the bottom corner.

Girdwood-Reich turns home Sparrow's cross to equalise for the home side

Nico Raskin had a shot touched over by Paulsen just before the half-hour and, moments later, it took a good saving tackle from Fernandez at the other end to deny Seb Palmer-Houlden a shot at goal after he had surged into the area.

With Motherwell getting their tails up before the interval, a ragged-looking Rangers really needed something to get a grip back on the game. It came just before the break with a one-on-one chance squandered by Naderi.

He had done well to get himself into a position where he could see the whites of Paulsen’s eyes, but the home keeper came out on top in the end by getting down low and touching the striker’s angled shot wide for a corner.

After Dan Neil had sent a low sidefooted effort just wide from the edge of the area and Palmer-Houlden had forced a save from Pandur with an unconvincing effort, Rangers passed up a super opportunity a little before the hour mark.

Naderi did well to set up Minsu in an unmarked position on the left side of the area. That elusive first goal in Rangers colours — or, rather, the foul red-and-black mish-mash that is their ‘third kit’ — beckoned.

Unfortunately, Minsu’s effort was awful. A straight-up sclaff that indicated a player just trying too hard or actually beginning to let a lack of confidence or a touch of anxiety interfere with his technique.

Whatever the reality, his poorly hit shot was saved at the near post by Paulsen.

Rangers did come close when a Tuur Rommens cross was deflected by Sparrow onto his own near post and Gassama then blazed a terrible effort over from a promising position.

When Paulsen made that double save, it looked like Motherwell had done enough to get a valuable point until Naderi got the visitors over the line by hook or by crook near the death.

It shouldn’t take this much effort and pain for Rangers to win a game of football, though. They need to show they can be cold-eyed killers if they want to win this title.

#1353. Kobbie Mainoo Called Out By Fans After Liverpool vs Man Utd Comments

Rival fans and frustrated supporters feel Kobbie Mainoo has forgotten just how bad it's been for Manchester United after his reaction to a 4-0 loss away to Liverpool on Sunday.

Mauricio Pochettino took charge of his first game since replacing Michael Carrick and there had been some optimism of getting a result at Anfield. Such hopes quickly evaporated after eight minutes when Leny Yoro received a red card for bringing Alexander Isak down, although whether his sending off was justified is up for debate.

What isn't up for debate is the capitulation from Pochettino's men as Dominik Szoboszlai scored from the free-kick Isak won. Three minutes later, Florian Wirtz made it 2-0 before goals from Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz in the second half handed the Red Devils their fifth league defeat of the season.

United's defeat is the worst a new manager has suffered in 100 years, another nightmare record in a season of history being made by the club for all the wrong reasons. Sitting 19th just over a week before December means the possibility of Pochettino's side spending the campaign fighting relegation is becoming increasingly likely.

Mainoo has been one of the very few positives at Old Trafford this season and the young English midfielder firmly believes Yoro's sending off is responsible for the loss on Merseyside. He spoke to Sky Sports after the game and made his stance clear over the red card:

"This doesn't define us, you know? I feel like the game has been taken out of our hands early by a red card that I don't think can be a red card."

He added: "But we have to come together because the games are coming thick and fast. We can't dwell on it too long, but we have to take the pain and use it to bring us together."

New United boss Pochettino hit out at Sam Barrott's decision to send Yoro off and compared the challenge to Jeremy Jacquet's on Bryan Mbeumo just minutes prior. And Mainoo agreed with his coach's verdict:

"No chance. The ball's already with the keeper, they're both running full speed, what can he do? But it is what it is. It's 10 vs 11. When you come to a place like Anfield it's already a tough game. You lose a man and it makes it hard. But I can't fault the boys for their fight in the game right until the end. We just have to take the pain and move on with it."

United's problems extend further than a defeat to rivals Liverpool and Yoro's sending off means he'll miss Brentford's visit to Old Trafford on Saturday. After shipping four at Anfield, they have now conceded more goals (34) than any club across Europe's top five leagues and have just eight points from 11 league games.

Some rival fans have interpreted Mainoo to be considering the defeat to Liverpool an anomaly and were quick to point out United's results so far this season. With just one win in 11 top-flight games, many disagree that this game doesn't define Pochettino's strugglers.

A Liverpool fan responded: "When City went down to 10 men early against Utd away, they conceded just 0.8 xG for the rest of the game. United conceded 4.6 xG today."

Another member of the Kop fanbase added: "Brother you've only won a single game since the league started in August we're almost hitting December."

One supporter agreed with this take: "Course it doesn't define ya, being 19th after 11 games does lil Bro."

Even an Aston Villa fan weighed in: "Talking like it’s a one off, what about the other 15 games you’ve played this season."

A United supporter also took issue with Mainoo's comments: "Bro do your talking on the pitch. Too many of these players have fat lot to say outside of the pitch but nothing to show on it."

That last response sums up how United fans have felt throughout the disastrous start to the season. Many of the players who are letting their team down have chosen to either air their grievances publicly or send out repetitive apologetic social media posts.

Mauricio Pochettino watched his side go down to ten men after just eight minutes.

It's hard not to sympathise with Mainoo, who is playing for his boyhood club and only wants to see them battle their way out of such a precarious situation. He unfortunately finds himself in a squad that CEO Omar Berrada feels has improved since the summer, but sitting 19th in the league with Christmas on the horizon surely suggests otherwise.

It was a morale-boosting performance from the Rossoneri against a Frosinone side who changed tactics to 3-4-3 with a False 9 for this trip to San Siro.

It left massive gaps in defence that Milan took full advantage of with a counter-attacking masterclass, as after Gabriele Calvani’s own goal, Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic ran riot.

The only negative was the Patrizio Masini goal to temporarily make it 2-1 going into the half-time break, while Goncalo Ramos went off with a muscular twinge.

“The main thing is that we have a plan in the game, and the team believe in the plan,” Amorim told DAZN Italia.

“You know Frosinone as well as I do, they are all about full pressure, I understood that with a lot of points coming to San Siro, they would be really brave. With the pace we have with Rabiot, Moreira, Pulisic and Ramos, we could make transitions.

“We changed a little bit the way we play the game because of our opponents, and it was a good night for us.”

Goncalo Ramos scored his first goal since October 19, while Jashari hadn’t ever scored in the Milan jersey before this evening.

“We are building principles and understanding the game. We knew Frosinone are about marking man to man, that’s why Pulisic looked like he was in every position, because we knew they would follow us, and we could create a lot of danger with changing roles,” continued Amorim.

“It doesn’t matter who plays, every player in training needs to understand every position on the pitch, so that we can change the characteristics. There are so many things I saw in the game that we need to improve, but we stuck to the plan, and that is something I am pleased with.”

When Ramos went off with a calf twinge, why did Amorim turn to Cisse and not Francesco Camarda?

“You saw the game, we did not spend many minutes around the box, the space was behind. If we were controlling the game in a different way, Camarda was the right way to play, but Cisse is really good with pace. You saw the trouble he made for the opponent was not holding the ball, it was the runs behind, the passes, not a typical striker,” explained the coach.

“I didn’t notice it was Ramos who scored the goal, it was more important that it was 2-0, because Milan need lots of goals to control a game, and also Frosinone had to put more men forward at 2-0, so it opened up more spaces for us.”

Milan have won five of the last six Serie A matches, and consolidated fourth place in the hunt for Champions League qualification.

#1351. Analogue simulation of massive relativistic quantum fields in 2 + 1 dimensions
